candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — evaluate medication response, recognize altered therapeutic effect, and safely manage IV vasoactive medications
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ephedrine tachyphylaxis during treatment of anesthesia-related hypotension
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize tachyphylaxis as a potential reason for diminishing blood-pressure response after repeated IV ephedrine doses and understand that ephedrine has mixed alpha/beta and indirect norepinephrine-releasing activity.

options.A: Repeated ephedrine administration can produce tachyphylaxis, so a diminishing pressor response may occur despite additional doses.
options.B: Ephedrine is a pure alpha1 agonist with no indirect sympathomimetic activity, so repeated dosing should always produce an identical response.
options.C: Ephedrine is a direct vasodilator, so a weaker pressor response indicates expected progression of its vasodilating effect.
options.D: The diminishing response proves the client has developed an immediate allergic reaction to ephedrine.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA/DailyMed labeling identifies ephedrine sulfate injection as an alpha- and beta-adrenergic agonist and a norepinephrine-releasing agent used for clinically important hypotension in anesthesia. The label specifically warns that repeated administration may cause tachyphylaxis, meaning a progressively reduced response can occur with repeated doses. B misstates the mechanism, C reverses the hemodynamic effect, and D assigns an unsupported diagnosis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Ephedrine has mixed direct alpha/beta adrenergic and indirect norepinephrine-releasing actions, and repeated administration can cause tachyphylaxis with a reduced pressor response.
candidate.source_locator: Indications and Usage — alpha- and beta-adrenergic agonist and norepinephrine-releasing agent for clinically important hypotension in anesthesia; Warnings and Precautions, Section 5.2 — repeated administration may cause tachyphylaxis and tolerance
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
candidate.stem: A client with anesthesia-related hypotension receives repeated IV ephedrine boluses. The nurse notices that later doses produce a smaller pressor response than earlier doses. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
